name: Apple Books
title: Return after exploration
observed: Apple documents returning to the earlier reading location and distinguishes automatic place saving from bookmarks. Its reading menu also exposes typography and scrolling choices.
proposal: Keep a saved reading position when Arabic or sources open. A bookmark should mean “return deliberately,” not “save my progress.”
limitations: Documentation review, not an iPhone walkthrough. The linked guide is for iOS 27; no assumption that every control matches the user's iOS 26.

name: Kindle
title: Flexible text, not a fixed page
observed: Amazon documents font, margin, spacing, alignment and page-colour controls, alongside assistive reading tools.
proposal: Preserve the comfortable 21px default and allow larger text without horizontal scrolling. Do not make reading depend on decorative canvas rendering.
limitations: Official feature description. Accessibility benefits were not independently measured; synchronized highlighting needs real timing data.

name: Kobo
title: One identity across formats
observed: Kobo's app description presents ebook and audiobook reading with several visual themes and saved reading continuity.
proposal: The current hadith should remain identifiable when the user moves between reading and listening; the theme should not change the information architecture.
limitations: Public app description only. Region redirects and intermittent fetch failures limit reproduction; no native-app flow was tested.

name: Libby
title: Progress at two scales
observed: Libby's player documents overall progress, chapter progress and a timeline with chapter breaks and bookmarks. Its timer documentation includes an end-of-chapter option.
proposal: Show the current hadith and the finite session separately. Finish on a whole entry; never cut off a narration to satisfy a nominal five minutes.
limitations: Official help review. This supports an interaction pattern, not a claim of better completion rates.

name: Foliate
title: Quiet chrome with a way back
observed: Foliate describes automatically hidden window controls, page or scroll reading, a contents sidebar and navigation history.
proposal: A direct reading view can be calm without removing source access. Keep explicit buttons for essential actions instead of relying on an undiscoverable gesture.
limitations: Official feature page and its documented flow; no Linux installation tested.

name: Readest
title: Reading and reference can coexist
observed: The web library supplied sample books. Opening one exposed a dedicated reading surface, bookmark action and separate appearance/navigation controls. Parallel reading is described on the product site.
proposal: Use a secondary source rail on wide screens. On the phone, open a full-width source panel and return to the unchanged reading location.
limitations: Limited browser interaction. The sample opened at its cover; settings and all pagination states were not exhaustively exercised.

name: Yomu
title: Defaults before customization
observed: Yomu describes fluid text layout, font and colour choices, page or scroll modes, and defaults saved per book.
proposal: Offer a short comfort panel and good defaults. Requiring the user to configure a reader before starting would defeat the purpose.
limitations: Product description, not installed-app testing. Testimonials were not treated as independent evidence.

name: Adobe Acrobat
title: Reflow is different from a scan
observed: Adobe documents a reading layout that reflows supported PDFs and exposes text and spacing adjustments without changing the original document.
proposal: Use semantic, immutable source blocks as the reading layer and keep the print witness accessible separately. Do not use live OCR as the canonical text.
limitations: Official workflow documentation. Reflow support is conditional and does not verify transcription accuracy.

name: PDF Expert
title: Phone reading has different needs
observed: PDF Expert's page describes text reflow for phone screens and reading themes, alongside a much larger editing feature set.
proposal: Keep the reflow principle and discard editing-tool density. Reference pages can remain faithful while the main text adapts to the screen.
limitations: Public feature description. No claim that every PDF or script reflows correctly.

name: LiquidText
title: Keep the route to the original
observed: LiquidText describes connections from notes and observations back to source context, and relationships across pages and documents.
proposal: Source inspection should retain the selected hadith and reading position. This does not justify adding a research canvas or extracted quote cards.
limitations: Public interaction description; no installed iPad or desktop session tested.

name: PDF.js
title: A document viewer is not the same task
observed: The live demo displays a printed research paper with page number, zoom, page navigation, search and editing tools. The paper's fixed two-column structure remains visible.
proposal: Retain exact edition/page references in sources, but do not ask the daily reader to pan around a miniature print page.
limitations: Desktop browser sample only; not a performance or accessibility benchmark of PDF.js.

name: Quran.com
title: Separate reading density from study density
observed: The verse-oriented view exposed repeated study controls and translation labels. Switching to Reading changed the presentation to a denser continuous Arabic view. A promotional overlay also competed for space.
proposal: Separate quiet reading from source inspection; retain obvious mode controls. Avoid overlays and repeated action rows in the narration.
limitations: Actual browser mode switch. Quran verse structure is different from hadith; do not split hadith into invented verse-like units.

name: Sunnah.com
title: Identity and provenance are structural
observed: The live entry places English and Arabic alongside book/chapter context and several reference systems. The reference footer distinguishes numbering conventions.
proposal: Use stable Bukhari identifiers and transparent witnesses. Make sources close but secondary, with one English reading column on the phone.
limitations: Visual browser inspection of the opening entry; no claim of permission to reuse its English translation.

name: Greentech Hadith
title: Hadith needs its own navigation
observed: Greentech documents last-read access, bookmarks, chains, grades and list/page modes. Its public page also promotes goals, streaks and selected gems.
proposal: Adopt hadith identity, full-chain access and continuity. Decline streak pressure and thematic selection because this user chose complete book-order reading.
limitations: Official feature-page study, not a native-app test. Do not transfer grading labels without a documented basis.

name: Sefaria
title: Sources next to the passage
observed: The official guide documents passage-linked resources and edition information. In the browser, a translation panel opened alongside the selected text, keeping the reading visible.
proposal: A modal source sheet on the phone and a rail on desktop can preserve context. Label the edition and translation status separately.
limitations: Actual panel-opening interaction plus help documentation. The browser panel remained loading in this sample; its detailed translation list was not verified live.

name: Readwise Reader
title: Action density should follow the task
observed: Readwise documents a quieter long-form view and vertical paged scrolling to avoid conflicts with selection and panel gestures. Its TTS help states that generated speech is unavailable offline.
proposal: Keep continuous scrolling and a concise action bar. Preserve pre-generated, checked audio downloads instead of adopting on-demand speech.
limitations: Official workflow documentation. Its product team's rationale is evidence of a tradeoff, not an independent usability study.

name: BookPlayer
title: A persistent listening surface
observed: BookPlayer's project documentation describes chapters, playback controls and listening outside the foreground app.
proposal: Keep the audio element alive while opening reading and sources. Show chapter boundaries, and avoid changing the file at each hadith in this sample.
limitations: Project README review; device-level behavior belongs to testing on the user's iPhone.

name: Pocket Casts
title: Make boundaries visible
observed: Pocket Casts documents chapter lists, navigation and timeline markers. The same guide distinguishes platform limitations and creator-provided versus generated chapter data.
proposal: Use only the existing measured hadith start times. Do not invent sentence timings or imply automatic chapter metadata is verified source structure.
limitations: Official documentation; native and web behavior differ. No claim that its audio system is interchangeable with ours.

name: Castro
title: An explicit upcoming queue
observed: Castro describes a queue whose items play sequentially and are downloaded for listening. It also offers skipping and silence processing.
proposal: Show the ordered upcoming hadith and the stopping point. Reject auto-skipping parts of a narration and unreviewed audio processing.
limitations: Public workflow description. Queue ownership transfers; content triage and episode skipping do not.

name: Serial Reader
title: Give a session an end
observed: Serial Reader offers daily portions of classic books with adjustable reading appearance.
proposal: Create a small, finite session in book order, ending at a whole hadith. The two-entry sample remains explicitly shorter than five minutes.
limitations: Public description, not a longitudinal habit study. Do not infer that daily locks, streaks or timed pressure improve this user's reading.
